_comment: What is in tests/fixtures/vision/live-training-20260908/, and what it is good for.
The FRAMES themselves are gitignored (same rule as every other clip here -- the repo tracks
annotations, not Supercell's pixels). This file is the tracked part: it says what was
captured, under what conditions, and which measurements came out of it, so a later session
can tell whether re-capturing is necessary.
FIRST LIVE CAPTURE OF THE DEPLOYED PIPELINE. Everything before this was recorded clips at
1920x1080; this is mss grabbing a 2560x1440 desktop through DeployCapture, which is the
venue: Nulls Brawl, Training Grounds (NOT a real match -- see caveats)
scene: hero at 8000 HP, four stationary training dummies at 4000 HP each, no projectiles

note: A DOWNSCALE, which is the good direction.
CORRECTED 2026-09-08. This field previously read 0.794 and blamed an overlapping window for
a second reading of 2521x1418. Both were wrong. 0.794 is 1126/1418 -- it was computed on a
LOBBY grab while normalized_source came from a GAMEPLAY grab, so the record mixed two
sources. 0.783 is 2002/2558 and 1126/1439, which agree, and which is what this row's own
The 2521x1418 reading is real and reproducible and has nothing to do with occlusion: the
Nulls Brawl LOBBY has a genuinely black 21 px band at the top of its own artwork, so
detect_content_box returns 2560x1418 there against ~2560x1440 in gameplay. Since the box is
computed once and cached, a loop started at the lobby would crop 21 real rows off every
gameplay frame. Fixed by not inferring at all -- DeployCapture.from_window takes the crop
rectangle from the window manager. See BRAWL_DEPLOYMENT_DESIGN.md 6.11.

files.f000..f039.png: 40 consecutive frames at a nominal 20 Hz, hero idle. The general-purpose set: gate, detector, HP, ammo, super.
files.before/acquired/hold00..hold19/idle.png: One joystick drive, bin 1 (right). `acquired` is the contact down at the anchor, `hold*` is the knob deflected, `idle` is bin 0 -- the knob back at the anchor WITHOUT a release. Good for reading the knob's own position off the framebuffer.

gate.note: refine() found its peak at the STORED radius -- unchanged. The radius transferred from the OBS recording to the live mss source on this setup, which is not something to rely on generally (see control_calibration.json's own note) but is what happened here.

capture_ms.note: machine was in use; the max is an outlier, not a steady-state figure

caveats: TRAINING GROUNDS IS NOT THE DEPLOYMENT VENUE, and two things differ in ways that matter.
1. The ARENA DOES NOT SCROLL. It fits on one screen, so the camera never moves and odometry
correctly reports ~0 tiles for every commanded direction. Odometry measures CAMERA motion.
Do not use these frames to test odometry, and do not read a zero here as a fault.
2. The BUTTON LAYOUT DIFFERS. The calibrated `super` and `gadget` anchors land correctly, but
the `attack` anchor at viewport (1748, 1042) lands on a green chevron button that exists
only in this venue, sitting on top of the real attack area. Taps there were unreliable: 2
of 3 consumed no ammo, and the super discharged without being commanded.
Per the operator, this is a VENUE artifact and not an aiming error: attack is an AREA,
not a button. Any tap on the right side of the screen fires so long as it misses the
Super and gadget buttons, and the attack stick floats to the touch point the way the
movement stick does. So the chevron swallowed a touch that was otherwise fine. The fix is
to pick the tap point by CLEARANCE rather than by the button centre, and to confirm it in
a friendly battle against the ammo counter.
3. The super appears permanently charged and the HUD carries `Edit Controls` / `Exit` buttons
and a `Damage per second:` readout, none of which appear in a match.
What these frames ARE good for: capture geometry, the match gate, the detector, both HP
readers, ammo and super reading, and joystick direction (which was measured on the hero's own
screen position rather than on odometry, precisely because of caveat 1).
